arrays:
📦 Array is a collection of elements stored in contiguous memory. 
🔹 All elements are of the same data type. 
🔹 Each element can be accessed using an index (starting from 0). 
🔹 Arrays allow fast access (O(1)) but insertion/deletion can be costly. 
🚀 Common operations include traversal, insertion, deletion, and searching.
strings:
🔤 String is a sequence of characters. 
🔹 Strings can be immutable (like in Python) or mutable depending on the language. 
🔹 Each character has an index. 
🔹 Common operations include concatenation, slicing, searching, and comparison. 
✨ Strings are widely used in text processing and pattern matching.
stack:
📚 Stack is a linear data structure that follows the LIFO (Last In, First Out) principle. 
🔹 The last element inserted is the first one to be removed. 
🔹 Basic operations include push (insert), pop (remove), and peek/top (view top element). 
🔹 All operations are typically O(1). 
🔹 Stacks can be implemented using arrays or linked lists. 
🚀 Common applications include expression evaluation, recursion (call stack), undo/redo operations, and syntax parsing.
queue:
🚏 Queue is a linear data structure that follows the FIFO (First In, First Out) principle. 
🔹 The first element inserted is the first one to be removed. 
🔹 Basic operations include enqueue (insert), dequeue (remove), front (view first element), and rear (view last element). 
🔹 Insertion happens at the rear and deletion happens at the front. 
🔹 All basic operations are typically O(1). 
🚀 Common applications include CPU scheduling, printer queues, buffering, BFS traversal, and request handling systems.
linked_list:
🔗 Linked List is a linear data structure made of nodes, where each node stores data and a reference to the next node. 
🔹 Elements are not stored in contiguous memory. 
🔹 Dynamic size allows easy insertion and deletion without shifting elements. 
🔹 Accessing elements is sequential, so random access is slower than arrays. 
🔹 Types include singly linked list, doubly linked list, and circular linked list. 
🚀 Common applications include memory management, music playlists, browser history, and implementing stacks/queues.
trees:
🌳 Tree is a hierarchical non-linear data structure made of nodes connected by edges. 
🔹 The top node is called the root. 
🔹 Each node can have child nodes. 
🔹 Common types include Binary Tree, BST, AVL Tree, Heap, and Trie. 
🔹 Traversals include Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder. 
🚀 Used in file systems, databases, and search engines.
sorting:
🔄 Sorting is the process of arranging data in ascending or descending order. 
🔹 Common algorithms include Bubble Sort, Selection Sort, Insertion Sort, Merge Sort, and Quick Sort. 
🔹 Efficient sorting improves searching and data processing. 
🔹 Time complexity varies by algorithm. 
🚀 Used in databases, ranking systems, and optimization tasks.
searching:
🔍 Searching is the process of finding an element in a collection of data. 
🔹 Linear Search checks elements one by one. 
🔹 Binary Search works on sorted arrays and is faster. 
🔹 Searching is fundamental in software systems. 
🚀 Used in dictionaries, databases, and navigation systems.
recursion:
♻️ Recursion is a technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller subproblems. 
🔹 Every recursive solution needs a base case. 
🔹 It simplifies problems like factorial, Fibonacci, tree traversal, and backtracking. 
🔹 Excessive recursion may cause stack overflow. 
🚀 Used in divide-and-conquer algorithms and hierarchical processing.
graphs:
🕸️ Graph is a non-linear data structure consisting of vertices (nodes) and edges connecting them. 
🔹 Graphs can be directed or undirected, weighted or unweighted. 
🔹 Common traversals are BFS and DFS. 
🔹 Representations include adjacency list and adjacency matrix. 
🚀 Used in maps, social networks, recommendation systems, and routing.
heap:
⛰️ Heap is a complete binary tree that satisfies heap property. 
🔹 In Max Heap, parent is greater than children. 
🔹 In Min Heap, parent is smaller than children. 
🔹 Common operations are insert, delete, and extract min/max. 
🚀 Used in priority queues, scheduling, and heapsort.
dynamic_programming:
🧩 Dynamic Programming is an optimization technique used to solve overlapping subproblems efficiently. 
🔹 It stores results of solved subproblems using memoization or tabulation. 
🔹 Reduces time complexity drastically. 
🔹 Examples include Fibonacci, Knapsack, LCS. 
🚀 Used in optimization and path problems.
trie:
🌐 Trie is a tree-like data structure used to store strings efficiently. 
🔹 Each node represents a character. 
🔹 Supports fast insertion, deletion, and prefix search. 
🔹 Commonly used in dictionaries and autocomplete systems. 
🚀 Used in spell checkers and search suggestions.
